Postgres cannot parameterise a DDL identifier, so a string must reach SQL here; INV-7's real question is whether that string can carry a payload. (i) By reading the mechanism: schema_name is always the output of schema_name_for_tenant/1, which returns {:ok, "tenant_" <> hex} only on the {:ok, canonical} branch of Ecto.UUID.cast/1. Reading deps/ecto/lib/ecto/uuid.ex directly: cast/1 has exactly three clauses -- a 36-byte string whose every non-dash position is passed through the private c/1 normaliser, a <<_::128>> raw binary, and a catch-all returning :error. c/1 (uuid.ex:116-138) maps only 0-9/A-F/a-f to lowercase hex and its final clause is `defp c(_), do: throw(:error)`, caught by cast/1's `catch :error -> :error`. issues.description: NEW FINDING (not ISS-0012..0017). Contract gap in Letflow.TenantProvisioning.replay_migrations/2: its default argument `migration_source \\ tenant_scoped_migrations()` is evaluated in the CALLER's context, outside the function body's own try/rescue. tenant_scoped_migrations/0 calls ensure_migration_module_loaded!/2 -> Code.require_file/1, which raises Code.LoadError if a manifest-listed file is missing from priv/repo/migrations/. So the 2-arity default path can raise instead of returning the @spec'd {:error, {:migration_failed, Exception.t()}}, while the explicit-argument path is fully covered by the rescue. Demonstrated with a minimal probe: `def f(x \\ boom())` with a try/rescue body -> f() yielded {:ESCAPED_THE_TRY_RESCUE, "default-arg evaluated"} while f(:given) yielded {:ok, :given}; and Code.require_file("does/not/exist_abc123.exs") -> {Code.LoadError, "could not load ... Reason: enoent"}. Deliberately NOT treated as an INV-8 failure: the filename source is a compile-time module-attribute literal list unreachable from tenant, user, or network input, the trigger is a build/deployment-integrity fault rather than realistic input, and the helper carries Elixir's `!` raises-on-failure convention. Suggested fix for a future requirement: move the default resolution inside the try (e.g. `def replay_migrations(tenant_id, migration_source \\ nil)` resolving nil to tenant_scoped_migrations() within the rescue's scope), or widen the @spec to name the raise. Non-blocking.

NEW FINDING (not ISS-0012..0017) -- doc drift in the authoritative security file itself, reported here per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's instruction to flag source-level discrepancies. docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md's INV-4 'How to verify' block specifies `grep -rn "System.get_env" config/ lib/ --include=*.ex` and a matching heuristic grep with the same --include=*.ex filter. Elixir config files are .exs, not .ex, so --include=*.ex can never match config/dev.exs, config/runtime.exs or config/test.exs -- i.e. the documented check structurally cannot inspect the very files INV-4's own Reference section points at ("config/dev.exs's bearer-token pattern (REQ-103) is the first concrete instance") or where DATABASE_URL is actually resolved (config/runtime.exs:11). The check as written has a blind spot on its own primary target. I compensated with supplementary --include=*.exs passes for this review (all clean, quoted in the summary), but the file should be corrected at the source to `--include=*.ex --include=*.exs` so a future reviewer following it literally is not misled. Non-blocking for this diff.

INV-4's documented heuristic cannot surface it (the value is 7 characters, below the regex's {8,} threshold), and config/ is untouched by this diff (empty `git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat -- config/`), so it is neither introduced nor worsened here and is not a gate failure. It is a throwaway local-container credential, not production secret material; flagged only so the record shows it was seen and assessed rather than missed by the heuristic. Any future change that promotes this config toward a real environment should move it behind System.get_env/1 per INV-4.
